items.title: 6.1.5 Equations of Circles Determined by Given Conditions (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 168-172: Cases 1-4 (three points; two points and centre on a line; two points and tangent; two points and touching a line); Examples 5-9; Figures 6.5, 6.6; Do You Know? box; determinant box

blocks.text: Ab tak humne dekha ke centre aur radius maloom hon to circle ki equation foran likhi ja sakti hai. Magar aksar sawal mein centre aur radius seedhe nahin diye hote; balke kuch sharten (conditions) di hoti hain: 'yeh circle in teen points se guzarta hai', ya 'yeh is line ko chhoota hai'. Aaj hum seekhenge ke aisi sharton se circle kaise dhoondte hain.

Kitab kehti hai: circle ki general equation \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) mein teen azad (independent) constants \(g\), \(f\) aur \(c\) hain. Agar equation teen di hui sharten poori kare to yeh teenon nikal sakte hain. Hum chaar alag cases dekhenge.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Circle ko poora pehchaanne ke liye theek teen numbers chahiyein (\(g\), \(f\), \(c\); ya centre ke \(h\), \(k\) aur radius \(r\)). Is liye teen azad sharten chahiyein. Har maloomat ek equation deti hai:
circle par ek point = ek equation; centre kisi di hui line par = ek equation; kisi line ko chhoona = ek equation (centre se line ka faasla = radius).
Yeh bilkul aisa hai jaise teen unknowns ke liye teen equations chahiyein; kam hon to bohat se jawab, zyada hon to aksar koi jawab nahin.

blocks.text: Case-1: A Circle Passing through Three Non-collinear Points

Agar teen non-collinear points (jo ek seedhi line par na hon) diye hon jin se circle guzarta hai, to general equation ke teenon constants \(g\), \(f\) aur \(c\) nikal sakte hain. Non-collinear ki shart kyun? Kyun ke ek seedhi line par pare teen points se koi circle nahin guzar sakta; circle aur line zyada se zyada do points par milte hain.

Ab Example 5 ko dhyan se dekhte hain. Is sawal mein teen points diye hain, aur na centre maloom hai na radius. Aise mein standard form lene ka koi faida nahin, kyun ke us mein teen unknowns \(h, k, r\) square ke andar phanse hote hain aur equations mushkil ho jati hain. General form mein \(g, f, c\) seedhe (linear) aate hain, is liye hisaab simultaneous linear equations ka ban jata hai, jo aap pehle se jaante hain. Yahi wajah hai ke teen points wale har sawal mein general form hi chuni jati hai.

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem: Find the equation of the circle passing through the points \((-3, 3)\), \((-1, 5)\) and \((5, 1)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: circle points \((-3, 3)\), \((-1, 5)\) aur \((5, 1)\) se guzarta hai.
Maloom karna: circle ki equation.
Tareeqa: Case 1. Sab se pehle general form (A) lete hain. Har point equation mein rakhne se \(g, f, c\) ki ek equation milti hai; teen points se teen equations, aur teen unknowns. Bilkul kaafi!

Step 1: Maan lijiye equation yeh hai
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 \quad \text{...(A)}\]
Kyun: centre aur radius maloom nahin; general form mein theek teen constants hain jo teen points se fit ho jayenge.

Step 2: \((-3, 3)\) se guzarta hai
\[(-3)^{2} + (3)^{2} + 2g(-3) + 2f(3) + c = 0\]
\[9 + 9 - 6g + 6f + c = 0\]
\[-6g + 6f + c + 18 = 0 \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Kyun: koi point curve par tabhi hota hai jab us ke coordinates equation ko satisfy karein. Dhyan dein: \((-3)^{2} = 9\), minus nahin.

Step 5: (1) mein se (2) tafreeq karein
\[(-6g + 6f + c + 18)\]
\[- (-2g + 10f + c + 26) = 0\]
\[-6g + 6f + c + 18\]
\[+ 2g - 10f - c - 26 = 0\]
\[-4g - 4f - 8 = 0\]
\[g + f + 2 = 0 \quad \text{...(4)}\]
Kyun: har equation mein \(c\) ka coefficient 1 hai, is liye tafreeq karne se \(c\) khatam ho jata hai. Phir \(-4\) se divide kiya. Dhyan dein: bracket ke aage minus har term ka sign badal deta hai.

Step 6: (2) mein se (3) tafreeq karein
\[(-2g + 10f + c + 26)\]
\[- (10g + 2f + c + 26) = 0\]
\[-2g + 10f + c + 26\]
\[- 10g - 2f - c - 26 = 0\]
\[-12g + 8f = 0\]
\[3g - 2f = 0 \quad \text{...(5)}\]
Kyun: phir \(c\) cancel hua; \(-4\) se divide kar ke (5) mila. Ab (4) aur (5) sirf \(g\) aur \(f\) ki do equations hain, jo hum Class IX se hal karte aa rahe hain.

Step 7: \(f\) nikaalein
\[\text{From (4): } g = -f - 2\]
\[3(-f - 2) - 2f = 0\]
\[-3f - 6 - 2f = 0\]
\[-5f = 6 \;\Rightarrow\; f = -\dfrac{6}{5}\]
Kyun: substitution (ek ki value doosri mein rakhna) se do equations ek equation ban jati hain jis mein sirf \(f\) hai.

Step 8: \(g\) nikaalein
\[3g - 2\left(-\dfrac{6}{5}\right) = 0\]
\[3g = -\dfrac{12}{5} \;\Rightarrow\; g = -\dfrac{4}{5}\]
Kyun: \(f\) ki value (5) mein rakhi. \(-2 \times -\frac{6}{5} = +\frac{12}{5}\), phir doosri taraf le gaye.

Step 9: (1) se \(c\) nikaalein
\[-6\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right) + 6\left(-\dfrac{6}{5}\right)\]
\[+ c + 18 = 0\]
\[\dfrac{24}{5} - \dfrac{36}{5} + c + 18 = 0\]
\[-\dfrac{12}{5} + c + 18 = 0\]
\[c = \dfrac{12}{5} - 18 = -\dfrac{78}{5}\]
Kyun: \(g\) aur \(f\) maloom hon to (1), (2), (3) mein se koi bhi \(c\) de degi. \(18 = \frac{90}{5}\), is liye \(\frac{12}{5} - \frac{90}{5} = -\frac{78}{5}\).

Step 10: (A) mein values rakhein
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 2\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)x\]
\[+ 2\left(-\dfrac{6}{5}\right)y - \dfrac{78}{5} = 0\]
Fractions hatane ke liye dono sides ko 5 se multiply karein:
\[5x^{2} + 5y^{2} - 8x - 12y - 78 = 0\]
Kyun: poore numbers wali shakal saaf suthri hai aur kitab ka aakhri jawab yahi hai.

Tasdeeq:
Har point ko aakhri equation mein rakh kar dekhte hain:
\[(-3, 3):\; 45 + 45 + 24 - 36 - 78 = 0\]
\[(-1, 5):\; 5 + 125 + 8 - 60 - 78 = 0\]
\[(5, 1):\; 125 + 5 - 40 - 12 - 78 = 0\]
Teenon points equation ko satisfy karte hain, jawab durust.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 5 ka 'game plan' yaad kar lijiye: (A) likho, teen points rakh kar (1), (2), (3) banao, do baar tafreeq kar ke \(c\) khatam karo, \(g\) aur \(f\) nikaalo, phir \(c\). Yeh har Case-1 sawal mein bilkul isi tarah chalta hai. Tafreeq karte waqt poori bracket ke aage minus lagana aur har sign badalna sab se nazuk qadam hai.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: Do points se be-shumaar (infinitely many) circles guzar sakte hain, lekin teen non-collinear points se sirf aur sirf ek circle guzarta hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ke is box mein teen points \((x, y)\), \((x_{2}, y_{2})\) aur \((x_{3}, y_{3})\) chhape hain. Pehla diya hua point \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) hona chahiye, jaisa determinant ki doosri row mein hai; \((x, y)\) to pehli row wala circle ka aam point hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh determinant kaam kyun karta hai? Pehli row ke saath kholein to \(k(x^{2} + y^{2}) + (\dots)x + (\dots)y + (\dots) = 0\) milta hai: yeh circle hai (ya line, agar \(k = 0\) ho, jo sirf collinear points mein hota hai). Agar \((x, y)\) teen diye hue points mein se koi ho to determinant ki do rows barabar ho jati hain aur determinant zero hota hai; yani teenon points is circle par hain.
Example 5 ke liye yeh determinant \(-4(5x^{2} + 5y^{2} - 8x - 12y - 78) = 0\) banta hai: bilkul wahi circle. Is liye determinant wala tareeqa jawab check karne ka bhi achha zariya hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Points \((0, 0)\), \((1, 1)\), \((2, 2)\) se circle kyun nahin guzar sakta? (Teenon line \(y = x\) par hain, yani collinear; circle aur line do se zyada points par nahin milte.)
Case-2: A Circle Passing through Two Points and Having its Centre on a Given Line

Is case mein do points diye hote hain aur yeh bataya jata hai ke centre kisi khaas line par hai. Do points se do equations aur centre wali line se teesri equation milti hai. Kitab ki misaal mein woh line \(y\)-axis hai, aur ek point khud origin hai.

Example 6 mein numbers ki jagah letters \(a\) aur \(b\) hain. Ghabraiye mat: tareeqa bilkul wahi hai, bas jawab bhi letters mein aayega. Aise sawalon mein sab se aham kaam yeh hai ke di hui maloomat ko foran istemal karein: centre \(y\)-axis par hai to us ka \(x\)-coordinate zero likh do; circle origin se guzarta hai to centre se origin ka faasla radius hai. In do baaton se aadha sawal hal ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem: A circle with its centre on \(y\)-axis passes through the origin and the point \((a, b)\). Find its equation.
steps:
Diya gaya: centre \(y\)-axis par hai; circle origin \(O(0, 0)\) aur point \((a, b)\) se guzarta hai.
Maloom karna: circle ki equation.
Tareeqa: \(y\)-axis par har point ka \(x\)-coordinate 0 hota hai, is liye centre \((0, \text{kuch})\) hai. Circle origin se guzarta hai, is liye centre se origin tak ka faasla hi radius hai; kitab isi liye centre ko \((0, r)\) likhti hai. Doosra point \((a, b)\) humein \(r\) ki equation dega.

Step 1: Centre se (a, b) tak faasla = r
\[r = \sqrt{(a - 0)^{2} + (b - r)^{2}}\]
Kyun: circle ka har point centre \((0, r)\) se \(r\) faasle par hai; yahi circle ki definition hai.

Step 2: Dono sides ka square le kar simplify karein
\[r^{2} = a^{2} + (b - r)^{2}\]
\[r^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} - 2br + r^{2}\]
\[2br = a^{2} + b^{2}\]
\[r = \dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2}}{2b}, \quad b \ne 0\]
Kyun: \(r^{2}\) dono taraf hai aur cancel ho jata hai, peechhe \(r\) ki seedhi (linear) equation bachti hai. \(2b\) se divide karne ke liye \(b \ne 0\) zaroori hai.

Step 3: Centre (0, r) aur radius r wali equation
\[(x - 0)^{2} + (y - r)^{2} = r^{2}\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 2yr + r^{2} = r^{2}\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 2yr = 0\]
Kyun: standard form lagayi; \(r^{2}\) phir cancel ho gaya.

Step 4: r ki value rakh kar fraction hatayein
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 2y\left(\dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2}}{2b}\right) = 0\]
\[b(x^{2} + y^{2}) - (a^{2} + b^{2})y = 0\]
Kyun: \(b\) se multiply karne se denominator khatam; pehle 2 aur 2 cancel hue.

Tasdeeq:
\[(0, 0):\; b(0) - (a^{2} + b^{2})(0) = 0\]
\[(a, b):\; b(a^{2} + b^{2}) - (a^{2} + b^{2})b = 0\]
Dono points equation ko satisfy karte hain, aur centre \(\left(0, \frac{a^{2} + b^{2}}{2b}\right)\) waqai \(y\)-axis par hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab centre ko \((0, r)\) likhti hai. Is mein yeh farz (assume) kiya gaya hai ke centre origin se upar hai (\(b > 0\)). Agar \(b < 0\) ho to formula negative value deta hai: centre \(\left(0, \frac{a^{2} + b^{2}}{2b}\right)\) origin se neeche hota hai, aur asal radius us ki absolute value \(\frac{a^{2} + b^{2}}{2|b|}\) hai. Aakhri equation dono soorton mein ek hi hai, is liye jawab par koi farq nahin.
Yahan Case 2 ki 'di hui line' \(y\)-axis yani \(x = 0\) hai, aur do points \((0, 0)\) aur \((a, b)\) hain.
Aur \(b \ne 0\) kyun? Agar \(b = 0\) ho to dono points \(x\)-axis par hain; un se barabar faasle wala centre \(x = \frac{a}{2}\) line par hoga, jo \(y\)-axis se tabhi milegi jab \(a = 0\), yani dono points ek hi hon. Is liye aisa circle mumkin nahin.
Case 3: A Circle Passing through Two Points and having Tangent at One of These Points

Is case mein ek line circle ko kisi point par chhooti (touch karti) hai, aur ek aur point bhi diya hota hai. Yahan ek nayi aur bohat kaam ki baat istemal hoti hai: jis point par tangent circle ko chhoota hai, wahan radius tangent par perpendicular hota hai. Socho cycle ka pahiya sarak ko jis point par chhoota hai, pahiye ki spoke wahan seedhi khari hoti hai. Is liye us point par tangent ke perpendicular line (normal) centre se guzarti hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar line \(x - 2y + 4 = 0\) circle ko \((2, 3)\) par chhooti hai, to kya \((2, 3)\) line par bhi hona chahiye? (Haan: \(2 - 6 + 4 = 0\). Hamesha pehle yeh check kar lijiye; agar point line par na ho to sawal mein hi ghalti hai.)

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.problem: Find the equation of the circle passing through \((1, 2)\) and touching the line \(x - 2y + 4 = 0\) at \((2, 3)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: circle \((1, 2)\) se guzarta hai aur line \(x - 2y + 4 = 0\) ko \((2, 3)\) par chhoota (touch karta) hai.
Maloom karna: circle ki equation.
Tareeqa: general form (A). Do sharten points \((1, 2)\) aur \((2, 3)\) se milengi (chhoone wala point bhi circle par hota hai). Teesri sharat tangent se: point of contact par radius tangent par perpendicular hota hai, is liye \((2, 3)\) par normal (tangent par perpendicular line) centre \((-g, -f)\) se guzarta hai.

Step 1: Maan lijiye equation yeh hai
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 \quad \text{...(A)}\]
Kyun: teen unknowns, teen sharten.

Step 2: \((1, 2)\) se guzarta hai
\[1^{2} + 2^{2} + 2g(1) + 2f(2) + c = 0\]
\[2g + 4f + c + 5 = 0 \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Kyun: point (A) ko satisfy karta hai.

Step 3: \((2, 3)\) se guzarta hai
\[2^{2} + 3^{2} + 2g(2) + 2f(3) + c = 0\]
\[4g + 6f + c + 13 = 0 \quad \text{...(2)}\]
Kyun: jis point par line circle ko chhooti hai woh circle par hi hota hai. (Line par bhi: \(2 - 6 + 4 = 0\).)

Step 4: Tangent aur normal ki slope
\[x - 2y + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow y = \tfrac{1}{2}x + 2\]
\[\text{slope of line} = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\text{slope of normal} = -2\]
Kyun: perpendicular lines ki slopes ka product \(-1\) hota hai: \(\frac{1}{2} \times (-2) = -1\).

Step 5: (2, 3) par normal ki equation
\[y - 3 = -2(x - 2)\]
\[y - 3 = -2x + 4\]
\[2x + y - 7 = 0\]
Kyun: point-slope form: point (2, 3), slope -2.

Step 6: Centre normal par hai
\[2(-g) + (-f) - 7 = 0\]
\[2g + f = -7 \quad \text{...(3)}\]
Kyun: point of contact tak ka radius normal ke saath saath hai, is liye centre \((-g, -f)\) normal ki equation ko satisfy karta hai; phir \(-1\) se multiply kiya.

Step 7: (1) mein se (2) tafreeq karein
\[[2g + 4f + c + 5]\]
\[- [4g + 6f + c + 13] = 0\]
\[-2g - 2f - 8 = 0 \Rightarrow g + f = -4\]
\[f = -4 - g \quad \text{...(4)}\]
Kyun: \(c\) cancel hua; \(f\) ko \(g\) ki shakal mein likh liya.

Step 8: f ki value (3) mein rakhein (substitute)
\[2g + (-4 - g) = -7\]
\[2g - 4 - g = -7 \Rightarrow g = -3\]
Kyun: (3) aur (4) mil kar sirf ek unknown chhorte hain.

Step 9: f aur c
\[\text{From (4): } f = -4 - (-3) = -1\]
\[\text{In (1): } 2(-3) + 4(-1) + c + 5 = 0\]
\[-6 - 4 + c + 5 = 0 \Rightarrow c = 5\]
Kyun: maloom values wapas rakh kar baaqi unknowns nikaale (back-substitution).

Step 10: g, f, c ko (A) mein rakhein
Ab \(g = -3\), \(f = -1\), \(c = 5\) ko equation (A) mein rakhte hain:
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 2(-3)x + 2(-1)y + 5 = 0\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x - 2y + 5 = 0\]
Kyun: yahi required circle hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[(1, 2):\; 1 + 4 - 6 - 4 + 5 = 0\]
\[(2, 3):\; 4 + 9 - 12 - 6 + 5 = 0\]
Centre \((3, 1)\), radius \(\sqrt{9 + 1 - 5} = \sqrt{5}\). Centre se line ka faasla:
\[\dfrac{|3 - 2(1) + 4|}{\sqrt{1 + 4}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{5}\]
Yeh radius ke barabar hai, yani line waqai tangent hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 7 mein kitab ne "Subtracting value of f in (3)" chhapa hai; sahi "Substituting the value of f in (3)" hai, yani f ki value (3) mein rakhna, tafreeq karna nahin.
Aakhri do lines bigri hui chhapi hain ("Thus, the required substiting the values of f, gernd c is equation (A) ..."). Sahi jumla: "g, f aur c ki values equation (A) mein rakhne se required circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x - 2y + 5 = 0\) hai." Kitab ka aakhri jawab durust hai.
Case 4: A Circle Passing through Two Points and Touching a Given Line

Aakhri case mein do points diye hain aur circle ek di hui line ko chhoota hai, magar chhoone ka point nahin bataya gaya. Yahan general form ke bajaye centre \((h, k)\) se kaam lena aasaan hai, kyun ke tangency ki shart 'centre se line ka faasla = radius' centre ki shakal mein seedhi likhi jati hai.

Example 8 se pehle ek nazar figure par sochiye: points \(A(3, 4)\) aur \(B(3, -4)\) bilkul aamne saamne hain, \(x\)-axis ke upar aur neeche. Jo bhi point in dono se barabar faasle par ho, woh lazmi \(x\)-axis par hoga. Yani hisaab shuru karne se pehle hi andaza ho jata hai ke centre ka \(y\)-coordinate zero aayega. Aisa andaza lagana achhi aadat hai: jab hisaab wahi jawab de to aap ko yaqeen ho jata hai ke raasta sahi hai.

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: Find the equations of the circles passing through the points \(A(3, 4)\) and \(B(3, -4)\) and touching the line \(x + 2y + 9 = 0\).
steps:
Diya gaya: circles \(A(3, 4)\) aur \(B(3, -4)\) se guzarte hain aur line \(x + 2y + 9 = 0\) ko chhoote hain.
Maloom karna: in circles ki equations.
Tareeqa: do sunehri baatein: (i) centre \(A\) aur \(B\) dono se barabar faasle par hai (dono radius hain); (ii) line circle ko tabhi chhooti hai jab centre se line ka perpendicular faasla radius ke barabar ho.

Step 1: A aur B se barabar faasla
Maan lijiye centre \(O(h, k)\) hai (yahan \(O\) centre ka naam hai, origin nahin).
\[|\overline{OA}|^{2} = |\overline{OB}|^{2}\]
\[(h - 3)^{2} + (k - 4)^{2}\]
\[= (h - 3)^{2} + (k + 4)^{2}\]
Kyun: dono faasle radius hain; square lene se roots se bach jate hain.

Step 2: k nikaalein
\[(k - 4)^{2} = (k + 4)^{2}\]
\[k^{2} - 8k + 16 = k^{2} + 8k + 16\]
\[-8k = 8k \Rightarrow 16k = 0 \Rightarrow k = 0\]
Kyun: \((h - 3)^{2}\) dono taraf hai, cancel ho gaya. Yani centre \((h, 0)\) hai: \(x\)-axis par, jo \(AB\) ka perpendicular bisector hai (A aur B bilkul aamne saamne hain).

Step 3: Radius
\[r = |\overline{OA}| = \sqrt{(h - 3)^{2} + (0 - 4)^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{(h - 3)^{2} + 16}\]
Kyun: (h, 0) se A tak distance formula.

Step 4: Centre se line ka faasla
\[\dfrac{|h + 2(0) + 9|}{\sqrt{1^{2} + 2^{2}}} = \dfrac{|h + 9|}{\sqrt{5}}\]
Kyun: point \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) se line \(ax + by + c = 0\) ka perpendicular faasla \(\frac{|ax_{1} + by_{1} + c|}{\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}}\) hota hai (Class XI / Unit 5).

Step 5: Tangency: faasla = radius, phir square
\[\dfrac{|h + 9|}{\sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{(h - 3)^{2} + 16}\]
\[\dfrac{(h + 9)^{2}}{5} = (h - 3)^{2} + 16\]
\[(h + 9)^{2} = 5[(h - 3)^{2} + 16]\]
Kyun: circle line ko chhoota hai; dono sides non-negative hain, is liye square karne se koi jawab ghalat nahin aata.

Step 6: Khol kar simplify karein
\[h^{2} + 18h + 81 = 5(h^{2} - 6h + 9 + 16)\]
\[= 5(h^{2} - 6h + 25)\]
\[= 5h^{2} - 30h + 125\]
\[0 = 4h^{2} - 48h + 44\]
\[h^{2} - 12h + 11 = 0\]
Kyun: sab kuch ek taraf laaye aur 4 se divide kiya.

Step 7: Factorise karein
\[h^{2} - 11h - h + 11 = 0\]
\[h(h - 11) - 1(h - 11) = 0\]
\[(h - 11)(h - 1) = 0\]
\[h = 1, \quad h = 11\]
Kyun: \(-12h\) ko \(-11h - h\) mein toda (product 11, jama \(-12\)). \(h\) ki do values ka matlab do circles.

Step 8: Centres aur radii
\[\text{centres } (1, 0) \text{ and } (11, 0)\]
\[r_{1} = \sqrt{(1 - 3)^{2} + 16}\]
\[= \sqrt{4 + 16} = \sqrt{20}\]
\[r_{2} = \sqrt{(11 - 3)^{2} + 16}\]
\[= \sqrt{64 + 16} = \sqrt{80}\]
Kyun: har h ko Step 3 ke radius formula mein rakha.

Step 9: Equations
\[(x - 1)^{2} + (y - 0)^{2} = (\sqrt{20})^{2}\]
\[(x - 1)^{2} + y^{2} = 20\]
\[(x - 11)^{2} + (y - 0)^{2} = (\sqrt{80})^{2}\]
\[(x - 11)^{2} + y^{2} = 80\]
Kyun: har centre aur radius ke liye standard form (Figure 6.5 dekhiye).

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{|1 + 9|}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{5}}\]
\[= 2\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{20}\]
\[\dfrac{|11 + 9|}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{20}{\sqrt{5}}\]
\[= 4\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{80}\]
Har faasla radius ke barabar hai, aur \((3, \pm 4)\) dono equations ko satisfy karte hain: \(4 + 16 = 20\), \(64 + 16 = 80\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Case 4 mein do jawab aana qudrati baat hai: do points se circles ka poora khandaan (family) guzarta hai, jin ke centres \(AB\) ke perpendicular bisector par hain. Aam taur par is khandaan ke do circles kisi di hui line ko chhoote hain, ek chhota aur ek bara. \(h\) ki quadratic equation yahi dikhati hai. Figure 6.5 mein dono circles dekhiye.
Ab kitab ki aakhri misaal: yahan circle ek axis ko chhoota hai aur doosre axis par ek khaas lambai ka tukda (intercept) kaat'ta hai.

Example 9 mein do nayi cheezein hain. Pehli: 'y-axis ko 3 units door chhoona' ka matlab hai chhoone ka point \((0, 3)\) ya \((0, -3)\). Doosri: 'x-axis par 8 units ka intercept' ka matlab hai circle \(x\)-axis ko do points par kaat'ta hai aur un ka darmiyani faasla 8 hai. Yeh faasla nikaalne ke liye roots alag alag nikaalne ki zaroorat nahin; quadratic ke roots ka jama aur product kaafi hain. Yeh chaal Class XI ke quadratic equations wale sabaq se aa rahi hai, use yaad kar lijiye.

blocks.title: Example 9
blocks.problem: Find the equation of the circle which touches the \(y\)-axis at a distance of 3 units from the origin and cuts off an intercept of 8 units on the \(x\)-axis.
steps:
Diya gaya: circle \(y\)-axis ko origin se 3 units door chhoota hai, yani \((0, 3)\) ya \((0, -3)\) par; aur \(x\)-axis par 8 units lamba intercept (chord) kaat'ta hai.
Maloom karna: circle ki equation (balke aise saare circles).
Tareeqa: jo circle \(y\)-axis ko \((0, 3)\) par chhooe, us ka centre horizontal line \(y = 3\) par hota hai aur \(y\)-axis se \(r\) faasle par. \(x\)-intercept un do points ka faasla hai jahan circle \(x\)-axis ko kaat'ta hai; yeh \(y = 0\) rakhne se bani quadratic ke roots ka farq hai.

Step 1: Centre dhoondein
Maan lijiye chhoone ka point \((0, 3)\) hai. Us tak ka radius \(y\)-axis par perpendicular, yani horizontal, hai. Is liye centre line \(y = 3\) par hai aur us ka \(x\)-coordinate \(\pm r\) hai. Pehle centre ko \(y\)-axis ke right mein lete hain:
\[C = (r, 3), \quad \text{radius } r\]
Kyun: point of contact par tangent radius par perpendicular hota hai.

Step 2: Circle ki equation
\[(x - r)^{2} + (y - 3)^{2} = r^{2}\]
\[(x^{2} - 2rx + r^{2}) + (y^{2} - 6y + 9) = r^{2}\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 2rx - 6y + 9 = 0\]
Kyun: standard form, phir \(r^{2}\) cancel.

Step 3: \(x\)-axis se milaap
\(x\)-axis par \(y = 0\) hota hai, is liye \(y = 0\) rakhein:
\[x^{2} - 2rx + 9 = 0\]
\[x_{1} + x_{2} = 2r, \quad x_{1}x_{2} = 9\]
Kyun: roots \(x_{1}, x_{2}\) woh jagahein hain jahan circle \(x\)-axis ko kaat'ta hai; roots ka jama \(= -\frac{b}{a}\), product \(= \frac{c}{a}\).

Step 4: Intercept ki lambai
\[|x_{1} - x_{2}| = \sqrt{(x_{1} + x_{2})^{2} - 4x_{1}x_{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{4r^{2} - 36}\]
Kyun: \((x_{1} - x_{2})^{2} = (x_{1} + x_{2})^{2} - 4x_{1}x_{2}\); roots alag alag nikaale baghair sirf jama aur product se kaam chal jata hai.

Step 5: Diya hua intercept 8 lagayein
\[\sqrt{4r^{2} - 36} = 8\]
\[4r^{2} - 36 = 64\]
\[4r^{2} = 100 \Rightarrow r^{2} = 25 \Rightarrow r = 5\]
Kyun: dono sides ka square; radius positive hota hai, is liye r = 5 (r = -5 nahin).

Step 6: Ek circle
\[(x - 5)^{2} + (y - 3)^{2} = 25\]
Kyun: centre (5, 3), radius 5.

Step 7: Symmetry se chaaron circles
Centre \(y\)-axis ke left mein bhi ho sakta hai, aur chhoone ka point \((0, -3)\) bhi ho sakta hai. Is tarah centres \((\pm 5, \pm 3)\) bante hain:
\[(x \pm 5)^{2} + (y \pm 3)^{2} = 25\]
Kyun: \(-r\) ya \(-3\) ke saath wahi hisaab sirf signs badalta hai. Dono \(\pm\) signs ek doosre se azad hain (Figure 6.6).

Tasdeeq:
\[y = 0:\; (x - 5)^{2} + 9 = 25\]
\[(x - 5)^{2} = 16 \Rightarrow x = 1, 9\]
Intercept \(9 - 1 = 8\). \(x = 0\) par: \(25 + (y - 3)^{2} = 25\) se sirf \(y = 3\) milta hai (double root), yani circle \(y\)-axis ko sirf \((0, 3)\) par chhoota hai.

blocks.alt: Example 9 ki exact graph, pale yellow panel par: magenta axes, -10 aur 10 ke ticks. Radius 5 ke chaar cyan circles, centres (5, 3), (-5, 3), (5, -3), (-5, -3); yeh y-axis ko (0, 3) ya (0, -3) par chhoote hain aur x-axis ko 1 aur 9 (ya -1 aur -9) par kaat-te hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Example 9 se teen sabaq milte hain:
1. Kisi axis ko chhoona ho to centre ka ek coordinate foran maloom ho jata hai: \(y\)-axis ko \((0, 3)\) par chhoone wale circle ka centre \((\pm r, 3)\) hai, yani centre ka \(x\)-coordinate radius ke barabar (sign ke saath).
2. Intercept (axis par kata hua tukda) nikaalne ke liye axis ki equation rakho (\(x\)-axis ke liye \(y = 0\)), quadratic banao, aur roots ka farq \(\sqrt{(\text{jama})^{2} - 4(\text{product})}\) se nikaalo.
3. Jawab dete waqt symmetry ko mat bhooliye. Sawal ne 'origin se 3 units' kaha, upar ya neeche nahin bataya, aur centre right ya left dono taraf ho sakta hai. Is liye chaar circles banenge. Figure 6.6 mein chaaron saaf nazar aate hain: jaise phool ki chaar pattiyan.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin.) Woh circle jo \(x\)-axis ko \((2, 0)\) par chhoota hai aur jis ka radius 3 hai, aur centre \(x\)-axis ke upar hai.
\(x\)-axis ko \((2, 0)\) par chhoone ka matlab: centre us ke bilkul upar, yani \((2, 3)\).
\[(x - 2)^{2} + (y - 3)^{2} = 9\]
Tasdeeq: \(y = 0\) rakhein: \((x - 2)^{2} + 9 = 9\), sirf \(x = 2\). Yani sirf ek point par chhoota hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh bhi hamari practice hai.) Teen points \((0, 0)\), \((4, 0)\) aur \((0, 6)\) se guzarne wala circle.
\((0, 0)\) rakhne se \(c = 0\). \((4, 0)\) se \(16 + 8g = 0\), yani \(g = -2\). \((0, 6)\) se \(36 + 12f = 0\), yani \(f = -3\).
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x - 6y = 0\]
Centre \((2, 3)\), radius \(\sqrt{4 + 9} = \sqrt{13}\). Dilchasp baat: \((4, 0)\) aur \((0, 6)\) ko milane wali line diameter hai, kyun ke origin par angle 90 degree hai (6.1.4 yaad kijiye). Centre waqai un ka mid-point \((2, 3)\) hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Circle ke teen constants hain, is liye teen sharten use pakka kar deti hain.
2. Circle par point: us ko general form mein rakho.
3. Kisi point par tangent: wahan ka normal centre \((-g, -f)\) se guzarta hai.
4. Line ko chhoona: centre se line ka perpendicular faasla = radius.
5. \(y\)-axis ko \((0, k)\) par chhoona: centre \((\pm r, k)\); \(x\)-axis ko \((h, 0)\) par chhoona: centre \((h, \pm r)\).
6. \(x\)-axis par chord: \(y = 0\) rakho; lambai \(= |x_{1} - x_{2}| = \sqrt{(x_{1} + x_{2})^{2} - 4x_{1}x_{2}}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Negative coordinates rakhte waqt sign ki ghalti: \((-3)^{2} = 9\) magar \(2g(-3) = -6g\).
2. Yeh bhool jana ke point of contact bhi circle par hai (Example 7 is point ko do jagah istemal karti hai: circle par bhi, normal par bhi).
3. Sirf ek circle likh dena jab sharten do (Example 8) ya chaar (Example 9) circles deti hain.
4. Distance formula mein modulus chhor dena aur phir koi jawab kho dena.
